title: 2026-06-10-crossroads-operating-deck-and-metrics-review
next_steps: Kemi to share trimmed operating deck and slide notes by 2026-06-14
People ops to publish Q3 hiring bands by 2026-06-18
Revenue to circulate updated ARR/usage scoreboard weekly starting 2026-06-17
Engineering to publish rollout plan for VPC beta by 2026-06-24
action_items: Kemi - Finalize 3-pager for Dedicated capacity product-market fit experiments - due 2026-06-14
Liam - Run latency percentile deep-dive and share root causes doc - due 2026-06-17
Jon - Validate disaster recovery RTO table for Dedicated clusters - due 2026-06-21
Priya - Coordinate case studies for two enterprise pilot customers and draft 1-pager - due 2026-06-30
summary: Leadership reviewed Q2 operating metrics, called out a mix of strong hosted adoption and slower Dedicated pipeline movement. Key themes: focus on reliability engineering to stabilize p99 latency, accelerating VPC/private GA work, and tightening hiring to mission-critical roles. Roadmap priorities were re-ordered to prioritize customer-facing reliability and security items over new product experiments for Q3. Multiple next steps assigned across Product, Eng, Revenue, and People Ops.
topics: Q2 growth metrics and usage trends
Private/VPC deployment roadmap and compliance status
Customer escalation and support ops improvements
questions: When will VPC GA be ready for SOC 2 customers?
How are we prioritizing quantization vs batching optimizations?
What is the contingency if a Dedicated customer needs air-gapped deployment?
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martinez: Okay good afternoon everybody, um, thanks for joining the Crossroads operating review. We're gonna run about an hour to an hour and a quarter, lots to cover — metrics, ops, and a few hard calls on prioritization.

[00:23] Kemi Adebayo: Hi all — quick housekeeping, slides are in the #all-hands channel, and we'll drop a slimmed deck after. I wanna start with topline usage: hosted API tokens up 28% QoQ, embeddings up 34%. That said, Dedicated offers conversion is lagging what we'd hoped.

[00:46] Liam O'Connor: On the engineering side, we've seen a small but persistent p99 blip with long sequences on the new 70b family. It's about KV cache eviction behavior under steady state and interaction with our batching heuristics. We're tracking but it's a priority.

[01:12] Audience (someone): Can you explain the KV thing again?

[01:18] Liam O'Connor: Yeah sorry, jargon. KV cache is where we store token caches for chat sessions — when it evicts too aggressively we re-compute long prefixes which spikes latency. We need a slightly different TTL profile for multi-tenant Dedicated pools.

[01:42] Alex Martinez: Thanks. Quick context — Q2 revenue is roughly on plan but back-half conversion from trial -> reserved is the bottleneck. Priya, you wanna take us through pipeline dynamics?

[02:00] Priya Rao: Sure. Pipeline dollar value is healthy but weighted towards POCs with security asks — many requests for VPC with dedicated throughput. Two prospects are holding for audit answers for KMS/HSM and for SOC2 readiness evidence. We're pushing faster on the security artifact deliverables.

[02:26] Alex Martinez: How realistic is VPC GA in July? We promised some customers mid-summer.

[02:31] Jon Park: Realistic with caveats — core control plane work is done, but integration tests with customer's KMS providers require more validation. Also, we need the DR playbook updated for isolated networks. I want an extra week for the migration test matrix.

[02:52] Kemi Adebayo: So that pushes a full GA to late July, early August if nothing unexpected shows up. We should be explicit internally about that timeline so sales knows what to tell customers.

[03:11] Alex Martinez: Okay, decision: prioritize VPC stability work, shift one product experiment slot out of core Q3 roadmap. We will keep one smaller experiment but not both.

[03:28] Engineering Q&A pool:
[03:33] [03:33] Speaker 1: For Dedicated, are we offering burst to hosted if capacity is low?

[03:38] Liam O'Connor: We have a fallback policy but we need clearer SLAs and opt-in language. Legal asked us to clarify cost/reliability tradeoffs.

[03:48] [04:00] Alex Martinez: Let's talk hiring — headcount will still grow but we need surgical hires: two SREs focused on runtime perf, one infra security engineer, and two sales engineers to support Dedicated POCs. People ops will freeze non-critical roles for 30 days.

[04:32] Kemi Adebayo: On product timelines, deprioritizing the multi-model orchestration experiment for Q3 and moving batching/quantization work forward. That aligns with cost/perf wins customers asked for.

[05:02] Audience (distant voice): Can you quantify the cost delta if we push quantization?

[05:07] Liam O'Connor: Preliminary internal numbers show up to 25% token cost reduction for 8-bit quantization with small model quality tradeoffs. We'll publish a model/quant table soon.

[05:27] Alex Martinez: Marketing and Customer Success — there were some notable escalations last month with two enterprise pilots. Kemi, Priya, you both worked closely on those. What did we learn?

[05:39] Priya Rao: Both were SLO and security conjcts — one needed finer tracing and request-level cost accounting, the other needed SAML integrations. We moved both forward but it highlighted a docs gap. We'll create a POC runbook.

[06:00] Kemi Adebayo: I'll own the runbook and the one-page checklist for sales to use during discovery.

[06:12] [06:12] Alex Martinez: Ops note — there was a near-miss earlier this quarter when a misconfigured autoscaler triggered undue preemption on Dedicated nodes. Jon, short summary?

[06:21] Jon Park: We had a rules misfire where burst policy cascaded; fixed mid-day but it surfaced a lack of canarying for autoscaler changes. We'll add an approval gate and a synthetic smoke test.

[06:40] Alex Martinez: Good. Ok next section — metrics deep-dive. Kemi please.

[06:45] Kemi Adebayo: We'll hit slide 12. Net retention looks healthy at 111% but that's driven by a handful of accounts expanding; median account growth is lower. Activation times for embeddings are down, which is strong. On churn, a couple of smaller customers left due to cost and underspec usage patterns.

[07:12] Speaker 2: Is pricing changes on the table to address cost churn?

[07:16] Kemi Adebayo: We're exploring usage tiers and adaptive discounts for committed Dedicated customers. Need revenue input.

[07:28] Priya Rao: We also need better signal in signup flows to capture workload type so we can recommend quantization or batching earlier. That will reduce sticker shock.

[07:42] Alex Martinez: Ok action item — add intelligent onboarding prompts to recommend cost-saving presets during trial. People ops and product to coordinate.

[07:54] [08:10] Alex Martinez: Let's surface some user anecdotes — we got good feedback from a startup customer who reduced latency 30% after following our batching recommendations. That shows we can drive immediate value with ops advice.

[08:30] Audience crosstalk: applause, laughter.

[08:40] Alex Martinez: On competition — yes, Anthropic and OpenAI are pushing products, but our differentiation remains predictable economics and private deployment options. We need to double down on the reliability story.

[09:02] Liam O'Connor: For that, metrics we publish externally have to be accurate — we will standardize p50/p95/p99 measurement and annotate model families.

[09:20] Speaker 3: Any update on the Dedicated reservation pricing experiment?

[09:24] Priya Rao: Running a small pilot with three customers to test monthly reserved capacity tiers; early signals look promising on stickiness. We'll report exact unit economics next week.

[09:38] Alex Martinez: Ok, finance note — burn is on plan for the quarter but runway extensions require careful deal structuring for Dedicated commitments. Work with legal to tighten terms.

[09:56] [10:10] Alex Martinez: Now open mic for 30 minutes, bring short remarks or questions. Please keep it brief.

[10:20] Speaker 4 (Engineering): Are we going to open-source the batching kernel improvements?

[10:26] Liam O'Connor: We will open-source parts but certain infra optimizations that leak customer patterns will be in internal repo. We need to balance community value and product defensibility.

[10:41] Speaker 5 (Sales): For the SOC 2 checklist, what's missing?

[10:45] Jon Park: The control evidence pack needs a few more artifacts: third-party pen test addendum, updated change control logs, and encryption-key rotation proof for KMS. Security team is on it.

[11:02] Alex Martinez: Ending recap: prioritize VPC stabilization and DR validation, move quantization/batching ahead of experimentation, hire 5 critical roles, tighten docs for sales/POCs. Kemi, Liam, Jon, Priya — you all own the primary workstreams.

[11:23] Kemi Adebayo: I'll share the slim deck and the short memo to managers so they can cascade.

[11:31] Alex Martinez: Thanks everyone. We'll run a follow-up on all action items in two weeks. If anything changes earlier raise in the #leadership-ops channel. Meeting adjourned.

[11:45] End of recording.
